root_cause.text: The pinctrl-mcp23s08 driver fails to explicitly clear the MCP_GPINTEN register during probe initialization, allowing stale hardware interrupt-enable states to trigger the interrupt handler before nested IRQ handlers are registered.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that commit f9f4fda15e72 changed the driver to read the real value of the MCP_GPINTEN register from hardware instead of using a bogus 0 default, revealing that the chip may retain interrupt-on-change features enabled after reboot; the patch resolves this by adding `mcp_write(mcp, MCP_GPINTEN, 0)` to disable all pin interrupts during initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disables hardware interrupts during probe initialization to prevent unhandled interrupt triggers before the IRQ subsystem is fully configured.
intent_record.what: Inserted code to write 0 to the MCP_GPINTEN register and added error handling to disable all pin interrupts before configuring the GPIO IRQ chip.
intent_record.how: Prevents the interrupt handler from executing for hardware interrupts that are enabled but lack registered software handlers during the driver probe phase.
